title: Autoware Index sweep result artifact
description: Schema for result.json, the per-repository artifact the sweep's validate job uploads (as validate-result-<ros_distro>-<repo_name>-<autoware_version>) and the record job's scripts/build_envelopes.py reads back. Emitted by the 'Compose result.json' step of .github/workflows/sweep-repository.yaml; both halves live in this repository so they change together. This constrains STRUCTURE: keys, types, and the outcome vocabulary. Semantic gates stay in the reader, which owns the diagnostics for them: an empty resolved_sha or autoware_version is a legal payload here and is skipped loudly by envelopes_for_row(), not rejected as malformed. Deliberately NOT additionalProperties:false at either level: an unknown key is a field someone ADDED, which the reader ignores harmlessly, and rejecting it would throw away a whole sweep's history over a backwards-compatible emitter change. A renamed key is still caught, by 'required' on the name that went missing. Exact key-set equality is asserted at PR time instead, by tests/test_sweep_repository.py.

schema.description: Artifact format version. Independent of the history record's own 'schema': 2 (schema/history-record.schema.json) — the two numbers coincide today and are versioned separately. find_result() gates on this, so bumping it without bumping the reader makes every artifact invisible rather than loud.

ros_distro.description: ROS 2 distribution the sweep ran for, e.g. 'jazzy'. Half of the identity find_result() matches a matrix row against; never copied into the record.

autoware_version.description: Autoware Core SemVer the packages were validated against, resolved at runtime by the latest-autoware-version action. Copied verbatim into each record's autoware_version, where history-record.schema.json enforces X.Y.Z. Empty means the resolve step produced nothing; envelopes_for_row() skips the whole row loudly rather than recording an unattributable version.

repo_name.description: Registry key of the repository entry. The other half of the find_result() identity match.

repository.description: Git URL the job actually cloned. Provenance only: the recorder builds record.repository from the matrix row, not from here.

ref.description: The ref the job actually checked out. Provenance only: the recorder builds record.ref_at_test from the matrix row, not from here. Mirrors distribution.schema.json#/$defs/ref, inlined so this schema validates offline.

resolved_sha.description: The exact commit that was checked out, 40 lowercase hex. Empty is the documented 'clone/resolve never completed' signal: nothing was validated, every package also carries present:false, and envelopes_for_row() skips the whole row on it. Left unconstrained here on purpose so that gate keeps owning the message; the recorder re-validates the 40-hex form via SHA_RE before it reaches a record.

packages.description: One entry per package name the job was asked to validate (the workflow's `packages` input). The recorder iterates the MATRIX ROW's package list, not this map, so a name here that the row does not list is ignored and a name the row lists but this map omits becomes a loud per-package skip.

propertyNames.description: ROS package name. Hyphens are legal in repository keys and tags but NOT in package names.

package_outcome.description: One package's verdict. Kept in $defs so build_envelopes.py can validate it per package: a drift here is attributed to the package it belongs to and skipped like any other inconclusive outcome, instead of dropping the conclusive records of every sibling in the same repository.

present.description: Whether `colcon list` found this package in the cloned tree. false means nothing was validated for it, whatever the outcomes say.

build_outcome.description: Verdict for this package's OWN workspace-local dependency closure, including a closure member declaring an unresolvable rosdep key. null means the build never ran (package absent, rosdep infrastructure fault, no-Summary infrastructure fault, cancellation) and is INCONCLUSIVE, never a red. The vocabulary is closed on purpose: status_for() compares against these exact literals, so any reword ('ok', 'passed', 'Success') would silently turn every package inconclusive and re-sweep the row forever.

test_outcome.description: Verdict for this package's OWN tests (colcon test --packages-select). null means the tests never ran, which includes the deliberate 'skipped' sentinel the emitter erases when the build already failed. Same closed vocabulary as build_outcome, for the same reason.
